lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: sleep and recovery routines

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 4: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice sleep and recovery routines. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A basic tidy routine only clears a space; a wind-down routine also helps a body get ready to rest.
safetyNotes: Share your three-step wind-down plan with a trusted adult before the first night so the adult knows what to expect.
If your routine includes dimming lights, adjusting a thermostat, or unplugging a device, check with a trusted adult first rather than changing household settings on your own.
This routine is about rest signals and steps only, never about how many hours you 'should' sleep or comparing your rest to anyone else's.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner cannot complete an overnight routine before this lesson is reviewed, they instead plan the same three-step wind-down routine in writing (a specific space-clearing step, a named rest signal, and a set start time) and describe, based on a typical recent night, which step would most likely have made the biggest difference, explaining their reasoning the way they would after actually testing it.

prompts.text: Explain what the rest-signal and consistent-timing steps added beyond just clearing your space, and whether you will keep using the full three-step routine.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Routine design specificity: All three steps are specific: a concrete space-clearing action, a named rest signal, and a set start time. | Morning follow-through and reasoning: The learner accurately compares how rested they feel and names which step likely mattered most, with a reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner test a second wind-down routine on a different night with the start time moved fifteen minutes earlier, and compare which of the two start times led to feeling more rested the next morning.

resources.title: sleep and recovery routines worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A basic tidy routine only clears a space; a wind-down routine also helps a body get ready to rest.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact sleep and recovery routines decision or action.
Model move 2: Before building your routine, think about a typical recent night.

Model move 3: Build a three-step wind-down routine for tonight: first, clear and prepare your sleep space the way you'd clear any space for a task; second, notice and name one body signal that tells you rest time is getting close, like heavy eyelids or a slower mind; third, pick a consistent time to start the first two steps.

Model check: Routine design specificity: All three steps are specific: a concrete space-clearing action, a named rest signal, and a set start time. | Morning follow-through and reasoning: The learner accurately compares how rested they feel and names which step likely mattered most, with a reason.

resources.title: sleep and recovery routines coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A basic tidy routine only clears a space; a wind-down routine also helps a body get ready to rest.
Coach direction: Before building your routine, think about a typical recent night.
Learner prompt: Describe what usually happens in the thirty minutes before you try to fall asleep on a typical night.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: sleep and recovery routines complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build a three-step wind-down routine for tonight: first, clear and prepare your sleep space the way you'd clear any space for a task; second, notice and name one body signal that tells you rest time is getting close, like heavy eyelids or a slower mind; third, pick a consistent time to start the first two steps.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote a specific space-clearing step for my sleep space, not just 'clean up.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named a specific body signal I'll watch for that means rest time is close.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I picked one consistent start time for tonight's routine.

Equal-access rule: If the learner cannot complete an overnight routine before this lesson is reviewed, they instead plan the same three-step wind-down routine in writing (a specific space-clearing step, a named rest signal, and a set start time) and describe, based on a typical recent night, which step would most likely have made the biggest difference, explaining their reasoning the way they would after actually testing it.

resources.title: sleep and recovery routines minimal evidence record

content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain what the rest-signal and consistent-timing steps added beyond just clearing your space, and whether you will keep using the full three-step routine.

Success checks: Routine design specificity: All three steps are specific: a concrete space-clearing action, a named rest signal, and a set start time. | Morning follow-through and reasoning: The learner accurately compares how rested they feel and names which step likely mattered most, with a reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: sleep and recovery routines supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional sleep and recovery routines condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Routine design specificity: All three steps are specific: a concrete space-clearing action, a named rest signal, and a set start time. | Morning follow-through and reasoning: The learner accurately compares how rested they feel and names which step likely mattered most, with a reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.
